title: Zener Clipper: A Diode That Caps the Peaks
topic: Zener diode used as a clipper / regulator — above the breakdown voltage V_Z it conducts in reverse and clamps the output to V_Z, shearing the tops off a sine input.

beats.narration: A diode that fights back when you push too hard — meet the Zener.

elements.content: Push too hard on a Zener — it pushes back at exactly V Z.

beats.narration: A Zener has an ordinary forward knee — but in reverse, it breaks down sharply at minus V Z and conducts hard.

elements.content: I-V plane: V on x-axis, I on y-axis, origin centred
Forward knee around +0.7 V rising steeply
Reverse knee at -V_Z dropping into negative current
V_Z label at the reverse knee

beats.narration: Wire a Zener across the output with a series resistor — once the input pushes above V Z, the Zener clamps the output and the resistor soaks up the rest.

elements.content: Source on left → series R → Zener to ground; output node between R and Zener
Zener diode symbol (triangle + bent cathode bar)
Labels: V_in source, R series, V_out across Zener

beats.narration: Feed in a sine wave taller than V Z. The output rides the sine where it stays below the clamp, but the peaks get sheared off flat at V Z.

beats.narration: The Zener acts like a voltage ceiling — anything above V Z gets clipped, anything below passes through unchanged.

elements.content: Below V Z: pass-through. Above V Z: clamp.
(a voltage ceiling — used for regulators, protection, reference)
